set.reason: Here a multiple means several copies of the same amount, and one criterion is writing it with multiplication. That is exactly the repeated equal-addend meaning of multiplication. Specific times-table facts are not needed.
set.scope: expressing several times a quantity by multiplication

set.reason: The product of three lengths counts cubic units. Interpreting the resulting volume requires cubic-unit meaning, without imposing all conversion drills first.

Computing solid volumes provides concrete experience of occupied space before considering what a container holds. The actual capacity meaning and liter/milliliter conversion can be learned by pouring measured liquid without a prism formula.
set.scope: meaning of capacity and the liter/milliliter rate

set.reason: Scaling length, width and height of a box shows the k^3 factor concretely. General solids follow by unit-cube approximation or similarity arguments, so it is supportive.
The square law is a natural analogy for the cube law and helps separate area from volume factors. The cube law can still be derived directly from unit cubes.
set.scope: contrast of square and cube laws

set.reason: Understanding that volume is measured in cubic units is essential to see why lengths scaled by k change volume by k^3. Detailed conversion skill is not essential.
The rule maps one length ratio to a cubed volume ratio, and inverse problems recover k from a volume ratio. Ratio meaning is central in every approach.

criteria: Check that the same length factor applies in all three spatial dimensions.
